newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico reserves, assets rise to Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico reserves, assets rise to Nov 22.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Tuesday its international reserves as of Nov. 22 were $16.257 billion, up from $15.801 billion on Nov. 15.
The central bank said that its net international assets on the same date were $4.725 billion, compared with $4.457 billion on Nov. 15.
It said the increase of $268 million in international assets in the week was due to:
- Net revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) of $213 million
- Purchases of $77 million from banks as a result of the exercising of dollar put options that had been placed by the central bank on Oct. 31.
- Net sales of hard currency to the government of $59 million, chiefly to cover debt servicing costs.

A net gain of $37 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts of commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said the monetary base fell by 818 million pesos due to a reversal in the seasonal rise in demand for notes and coins the week before.

The balance of the government's deposits with the central bank rose by a net 6.782 billion pesos, mainly as a result of tax collection minus transfers to federal dependencies and withdrawals to service foreign debt.
Central bank credit to financial institutions rose by 3.168 billion pesos to compensate for the monetary impact of a contraction of liquidity coming from an increase of government deposits.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six month duration from other central banks.
